diagnostic_evidence.quote: While not identical to classical Chebyshev points, such nodes exhibit the same characteristic clustering near the interval endpoints.
It is a well-established result in approximation theory that the Lebesgue constant for polynomial interpolation at these nodes exhibits logarithmic growth

issues.failure_explanation: The proof reduces the bound to polynomial interpolation at nodes \xi_k=\cos\theta_k. For fixed \delta>0, \theta_k lie in [\theta_min,\pi-\theta_min] with \theta_min>0, so d\xi/d\theta=-\sin\theta is bounded below by \sin\theta_min>0. The \xi_k are therefore quasi-uniform interior nodes, not Chebyshev nodes with endpoint clustering, and the cited logarithmic Lebesgue-constant result does not apply to them.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the false quasi-uniform-node claim with a valid Lebesgue bound for these nodes or restrict to genuinely Chebyshev collocation points, which changes the advertised stability scope.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised logarithmic stability of the one-dimensional basis interpolation, and the tensor-product version built from it, are not established and the logarithmic bound is materially false as written.
issues.title: False logarithmic Lebesgue bound for uniform sine-basis interpolation
issues.why_classification: The repair cannot preserve the stated logarithmic guarantee on the method's uniform grid; the stability type for the basis result would have to be weakened or the node choice changed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The matrix $\mat{W}(\delta)$, when scaled, converges to $\mat{M}$.
The smallest singular value $\sigma_{\min}(\mat{W}(\delta))$ must tend to zero.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof shows only that the scaled collocation matrix tends to a singular limit, so \sigma_min(W(\delta))\to0. The Lebesgue functions are combinations of the basis functions w_k, whose sup norms vanish like \delta^{-1/2}. Without a rate for \sigma_min or a direct lower bound for the Lagrange functions, \sigma_min\to0 does not imply the Lebesgue constant diverges.

failure_location.quote: The Lebesgue constant, which depends on the norm of the inverse of the collocation matrix, must therefore be unbounded as $\delta \to \infty$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a direct construction of data/functions with bounded sup norm but large interpolant, or estimate the decay rate of \sigma_min(W(\delta)) sufficiently fast relative to \delta^{-1/2}; this is a contained local proof repair.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem that the basis Lebesgue constant is unbounded as \delta\to\infty for fixed N\ge3 is unsupported as proved.
issues.title: Missing rate linking singular collocation matrix to Lebesgue blow-up
issues.why_classification: The conclusion may survive, but the source lacks a nontrivial estimate; fixing it is local and does not change the main Poisson/convection results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We can assume without loss of generality that $\alpha$ is an irrational number.
The coefficients $a_j$ in the continued fraction expansion are unbounded for almost all real numbers $\alpha$.

issues.failure_explanation: If the lemma held, then for large N_j each \theta_k/\pi would be within O(e^{-cN_j}) of an integer. Consecutive values differ by N L/((N-1)(L+2\delta)), which tends to \beta=L/(L+2\delta)\in(0,1/2); hence for large N this difference is a positive distance away from every integer, contradicting the exponential closeness to integers for all k. The appendix additionally assumes irrationality and almost-all behavior not justified by the fixed-parameter statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the integral is bounded by $C/K$ for a constant $C$ that depends on the geometry ($L, \delta, a, b$) but not on the degree $M$.

issues.failure_explanation: A degree-independent local-to-global L2 inequality for trigonometric polynomials on nested intervals is false. High-degree Fejér-type kernels can be concentrated in the extension strip, making ||g||_{L2(tilde I)} grow with degree while ||g||_{L2(I)} remains small/bounded. The appendix's key estimate \int_{J1}\sum|\ell_j|^2 \le C_geom/K is likewise false for extrapolating polynomial interpolation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish a valid local-to-global inequality (or accept degree-dependent constants) and rederive the stability estimates, which may destroy the polynomial guarantee.
issues.overall_effect: The continuous-to-extended-domain norm bridge used to prove discrete stability for constant, variable, and dD convection-diffusion is invalid.
issues.title: False uniform L2 norm-equivalence between physical and extended domains
issues.why_classification: The false lemma is a central dependency for the main stability theorems; replacing it is not a local correction and the advertised polynomial stability may be lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For functions in the space containing $\{L[u_N]\}$, which have degree $M=O(N)$, an equivalence between the discrete and continuous $L^2$ norms holds.

issues.failure_explanation: For the N collocation angles \theta_i, the function T(\theta)=\prod_{i=1}^N \sin(\theta-\theta_i) is a nonzero trigonometric polynomial of degree N that vanishes at every collocation point. Thus its discrete sum is zero while its L2(I) norm is positive, so no c_1'>0 independent of N can satisfy the stated inequality for degree O(N) trigonometric polynomials.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove a specialized discrete-continuous equivalence for the actual N-dimensional collocation subspace or change the sampling/norm, then reprove the \sigma_min lower bound.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete-to-continuous L2 lower bound needed to control \sigma_min(A) is false; the polynomial Lebesgue stability theorems are unsupported.
issues.title: False uniform discrete-continuous L2 equivalence for collocation grid
issues.why_classification: This is a central bridge in all convection-diffusion stability proofs; the stated uniform equivalence is directly contradicted by a nonzero vanishing trigonometric polynomial.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If the convection coefficient $k(x) \in C^1(\tilde{I})$ satisfies the condition $\norm{k'}_{L^\infty(\tilde{I})} < 2/C_P^2$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem assumes k\in C^1(I) but imposes \|k'\|_{L^\infty(\tilde I)} and invokes the coercivity lemma, which requires k\in C^1(\tilde I). As written, k' is not defined on the extension domain \tilde I.

failure_location.quote: Let the convection coefficient $k(x) \in C^1(I)$ satisfy the coercivity condition $\norm{k'}_{L^\infty(\tilde{I})} < 2/C_P^2$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the hypothesis to k\in C^1(\tilde I) (or specify an extension of k to \tilde I) so that the invoked coercivity lemma applies; this is a local correction.
issues.overall_effect: The variable-coefficient stability theorem has an ill-defined hypothesis/proof dependency.
issues.title: Variable-coefficient theorem assumes k on I but uses k' on extended domain
issues.why_classification: A single forced domain correction removes the inconsistency and preserves the substantive variable-coefficient claim, assuming the other stability ingredients are repaired.
